subject: Urgent: Finovata experiencing p95/p99 spikes — cold-start pattern, need exec visibility
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finovata.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: support@redwood.com
Date: 2027-07-02T08:15:00Z
Subject: Realtime API degraded — p95/p99 spikes starting 08:05 UTC

Camila / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden degradation in our production calls to the Hosted API starting ~08:05 UTC. p95 jumped from ~180ms to 2.4s and p99s are hitting 7–9s intermittently. Throughput dropped ~25% as a result. Error rate (5xx) rose to 1.8% during the windows. This is causing timeouts for our synchronous flows.

I've attached a small telemetry dump (finovata_telemetry_20270702.csv) which shows the request timestamps, response latencies, and the instance IDs in the response metadata. Note the spikes correlate with first-request-after-idle patterns — several traces show the first token taking multiple seconds.

Can you confirm whether this is an autoscaler/cold-start issue on your side? Customer impact: checkout/authorization calls are failing intermittently. We're happy to jump on a call — please advise next steps and ETA to stabilize.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Reliability
Finovata

Attachments: finovata_telemetry_20270702.csv (CSV, 72 KB)

Subject: Re: Realtime API degraded — p95/p99 spikes starting 08:05 UTC

Quick update from the infra side after an initial pass on the autoscaler logs and GPU pool telemetry:

- Observed multiple "instance-init" events for pool hosted-gpu-pool-us-east-2 between 08:03:20 and 08:07:12 UTC. Average instance spin time ~23s, but a tail of instances took 68–74s to finish bootstrapping (kernel selection + model mmap).
- Warm-pool utilization was 0 for several minutes prior to the spike — requests arriving after idle had to trigger fresh allocations (cold chain).
- There's a correlation between the instance IDs in Finovata's telemetry and our bootstrap logs. I flagged INF-1129 (link: https://jira.redwood/browse/INF-1129) as related.
- No clear evidence of model corruption; it's the cold-start path (kernel JIT + weights mmap + KV cache priming) causing the long tail.

Immediate mitigations I can do:
1) Force-allocate a small warm pool (temp: +3 instances) for Finovata's route and pin the model variant with faster mmap (quantized variant) for the next 1 hour.
2) Enable an aggressive prefix/KV caching bypass to avoid additional work on first request.

Impact/risks: 1) will increase short-term cost on the pool; 2) switching to quantized variant may have subtle quality delta (should be minimal for their prompts).

I'll stand by on the bridge.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE — Serving Runtime

Liam — thank you for raising this. We absolutely understand the priority.

Proposed immediate customer-facing actions (for your approval):
- Redwood will temporarily increase the warm pool for your main route by +3 instances in us-east-2 and route traffic to a quantized variant with lower mmap times.
- We will issue a one-time service credit for the impacted hour and extend monitoring with 12-hour elevated telemetry retention so you can validate.
- Schedule: we can start the warm-pool increase at 08:40 UTC and monitor for 30–60 minutes, then revert to baseline if stable.

If that plan is acceptable we will proceed now. Apologies again for the interruption — we'll keep you updated every 10 minutes on the bridge.

Subject: Exec visibility: Finovata production p95/p99 regression due to cold-starts — request emergency approval for warm-pool rollout

Aditya — raising for executive visibility because Finovata is a mid-sized customer with a usage pattern that drove a near-prod outage for their checkout flow. Summary:
- Impact: p95 increased to ~2.4s and p99 spikes to 7–9s for ~15 minutes starting 08:05 UTC; 5xx rose to 1.8%; throughput dropped ~25%.
- Root cause (prelim): autoscaler allowed the pool to go fully idle; cold-start path (kernel selection + mmap + KV priming) produced long tail spin times (up to ~74s). See INF-1129.
- Proposed immediate mitigations (Rishi): force warm-pool +3, route to quantized variant, enable aggressive prefix caching.
- Customer remediation: Marissa has proposed a one-time credit + elevated telemetry retention.

Requesting your approval to enact the mitigations now and to authorize the short-term increased spend and model-variant switch. Also seeking guidance on whether we should:
- Trigger a post-mortem with infra/product within 48 hours, and
- Prioritize a warmed-reservation feature for customers with synchronous SLAs (we can discuss trade-offs).

I'll be on the bridge and will update you with minutes.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com
